ImageDescription.value:
Japanese WW2 era Tankette Manufacturer:- Hiro Motor Co Built:- 1934 to 1937 Total Production:- 596 Main Armament:- 6.5mm Type 91 machine gun In service from 1934 until August 1945 when Soviet forces invaded Manchukuo. This example is one recovered from that last action and is now on display in Hall 12 of the Patriot Museum Complex. Park Patriot, Kubinka, Moscow Oblast, Russia.

25th August 2017

primaryTechnicalSources.kind: Wartime US intelligence; approximate identification and dimensions
primaryTechnicalSources.tableScope: Model 92 table describes the early small-idler configuration; Model 94 prose describes later trailing idler and lowered drive sprocket

primaryTechnicalSources.title: Japanese Military Forces No16, Japanese Weapons and Equipment PartI; Allied Land Forces SEAsia, GHQ India Intelligence Directorate
primaryTechnicalSources.kind: Contemporary Allied recognition handbook, not an engineering survey
primaryTechnicalSources.supports: Early small-idler description under Type92 nomenclature; four road wheels in two bogies, bell cranks and protected horizontal helical spring
primaryTechnicalSources.limits: Its later Type94 paragraph describes the trailing-idler form. No measured wheel spacing, cab yaw or museum dimensions are supplied; Japanese provisional nominal dimensions retain precedence
